description:
Currently each extension-server defines a concrete-typed copy_X method:
- MailBackend::copy_email(card: Email)
- ContactsBackend::copy_contact_card(card: ContactCard)

The other write methods on the same traits (create_object, update_object, destroy_object) are generic over O: SetObject. The /copy method's concrete type ties the trait to the specific extension type crate (jmap-mail-types, jmap-contacts-types) and prevents the workspace from later splitting wire-type vs domain-type, cutting a types-crate major version, or unifying /copy across extensions.

Recommended shape (from JMAP-qz9v.34):

  fn copy_object<O: SetObject + Send + Sync>(
      &self,
      caller: &Self::CallerCtx,
      from_account_id: &Id,
      to_account_id: &Id,
      obj: O,
  ) -> impl Future<Output = Result<(Id, O), BackendSetError<Self::Error>>> + Send;

The canonical-template propagation rule applies: change canonical mail-server first, then propagate to contacts-server (and any future /copy extension siblings like calendars-server, tasks-server).

Open questions:
- Does generalizing break any backend-side type-specific logic (e.g. mail-server's blob handling on Email/copy)? Should /copy stay type-specific because the conversion logic IS type-specific?
- Is the foundation JmapBackend supertrait the right home for copy_object, or should each extension trait carry its own?
- Pre-1.0 (workspace is 0.1.x), so breaking the trait surface is acceptable; post-1.0 this would require a major bump.

Workspace-design call. P3 because the current shape is internally cookie-cutter-consistent across extension-servers and the version-skew failure is hypothetical pre-1.0.
title: Workspace design: generalize ContactsBackend::copy_contact_card / MailBackend::copy_email to JmapBackend::copy_object<O: SetObject>
